steps.label: Classify the intent
steps.human:
Jev classifies the unchanged goal using compact entity meanings and separate caller claims; an explicit contract still controls routing, and only unresolved intent or a necessary choice requires clarification.

The input binding is the internal EntityContext checkpoint passed to intent, not the JSON sent verbatim to Jev. kernel/entity_projection.py creates a bounded meaning projection, with caller_context and registered_capabilities in separate channels; clarifications travel separately from the unchanged goal. The projection can add trust and occurrence counts and shorten retained matches, so it is not an EntityContext DTO. ChoiceAnswer is the provider result; the kernel applies it to root routing. An explicit requested_output_schema can skip inference. Source: kernel/intent/classify.py and kernel/intent/step.py.

steps.label: Spot a compound subject
steps.human:
At routing, the subject is checked for several separate questions bundled together. A bundled subject is offered as a split whether no capability matched it (jev_none), routing could not choose one capability for it (ambiguous), or routing would accept it as one decision (bundled_accepted). A no-match alone does not make a subject compound.

Design only (DK-400a, DK-400b; ADR-067 not yet written). The checked inputs are today's: TaskInput.goal, which the split record keeps as subject_text with whitespace runs collapsed, and the routing ChoiceAnswer that interpret_answer in kernel/scheduler/routing.py maps to no_match (reason jev_none), insufficient_context (jev_needs_context or low_confidence) or a selection; an insufficient_context intent answer (kernel/intent/classify.py) is the other ambiguous source. The RoutingAssessment that records the outcome is not an allowlisted contract, so the answer it interprets is bound. The bundle judgement and the split record are not built.

The split-answer payload waits for ADR-067, so the submission example omits response_schema_id and response.

steps.label: Run the parts in order
steps.human:
The approved parts run one at a time as children of this run, in dependency order. A decision part goes through the steps that follow, from precedent to resolve; a research part runs as a research child. An earlier part's result is precedent for the later ones.

Design only (DK-400e; ADR-067 not yet written). Parts become child work items of the split item in the same run, bound to their approved child_capability (decision or research, both registered at 1.0.0) without a routing Jev call. A decided part's result is today's DecisionReportPayload from the decision capability, and an answered part's is today's EvidenceBundlePayload from research; parts run inside one run, so no part has a RunEnvelope of its own. Which accepted payload a part's request carries (goal_request.v1, decision_request.v1 or research_request.v1) is not settled.

acceptance_scenarios.given: same-spelling names across namespaces, generic prose, overlapping phrases, duplicate short symbol names and a qualified symbol reference
acceptance_scenarios.when: deterministic owner-declared matching and resolution run
acceptance_scenarios.then: boundary-sensitive and type-cued matching excludes false hits, repeated identities deduplicate, bounded ambiguities remain unresolved, and qualification selects the exact permitted symbol

acceptance_scenarios.given: valid but absent IDs, malformed IDs, unsupported-language symbols and a new feature name
acceptance_scenarios.when: recognition resolves against canonical owner syntax and scoped index membership
acceptance_scenarios.then: explicit references retain unknown, invalid or unsupported states without fabricated meaning, full artifact reads or automatic human clarification

acceptance_scenarios.given: denied paths, narrow read roots, a symlink escape, sensitive values and an index built under broader permissions
acceptance_scenarios.when: the index is filtered before matching or disclosing metadata
acceptance_scenarios.then: names, existence, titles, paths, signatures and hashes of forbidden entries are withheld; caller claims and source meanings remain separate untrusted data without granting authority

acceptance_scenarios.given: an explicit output contract or a resumed human or host interaction
acceptance_scenarios.when: intake or resume proceeds under the contract
acceptance_scenarios.then: new tasks receive recognition without changing their explicit contract, while resumed tasks reuse checkpointed interpretation context and later evidence records separate snapshot provenance

acceptance_scenarios.given: checkpointed interpretation context with changed source files or optional context exceeding a provider budget
acceptance_scenarios.when: later native judgments or host work consume its projection
acceptance_scenarios.then: meaning provenance remains distinct from task evidence, changed snapshots remain visible, optional context fits the exact remaining receiver budget, and the original goal and full admitted checkpoint stay intact

acceptance_scenarios.given: a labeled entity corpus with ordinary prose, long inputs, aliases, symbols, IDs and adversarial definitions
acceptance_scenarios.when: the recognition-only evaluation and a separate paired intent evaluation run
acceptance_scenarios.then: case-level checks report identity precision and recall by family, ambiguity, provenance, permissions, bounds and actual lookup work; historical DK-200 tests are not treated as proof of the new design

acceptance_scenarios.given: a missing, stale, invalid or partly unsupported index, disabled recognition or an exhausted bound
acceptance_scenarios.when: the initial pass finishes
acceptance_scenarios.then: recognized, no_matches, partial, unavailable or disabled describes its actual coverage; no crawl, BM25, embeddings, wildcard fallback or synchronous full index rebuild occurs before intent

acceptance_scenarios.given: the unchanged goal, compact entity meanings, separate caller claims and unresolved references
acceptance_scenarios.when: Jev classifies intent
acceptance_scenarios.then: an explicit contract wins; unknown new entities can still route as change, and definitions do not prove runtime availability, user preference, approval or task completion

acceptance_scenarios.given: a classified decision goal and entity meanings containing canonical references
acceptance_scenarios.when: the routed capability needs evidence
acceptance_scenarios.then: references guide targeted retrieval after intent; AC criteria, function bodies, relations and precedent are read only as needed and meanings never substitute for supporting evidence

acceptance_scenarios.given: a natural-language evidence need with permitted canonical IDs or trusted component context and a configured graph read source
acceptance_scenarios.when: Jev selects among executable offered operations and a permitted repository fallback or unsupported outcome
acceptance_scenarios.then: trusted code binds and validates bounded arguments, confidence, remaining budget and pinned access scope before execution; returned evidence retains actual request and source provenance

acceptance_scenarios.given: an explicit operation request, an ordinary repository question or a request for every ticket with high or critical priority without a supporting exhaustive graph operation
acceptance_scenarios.when: the retrieval route is selected
acceptance_scenarios.then: explicit operation requests avoid the new selector; permitted repository retrieval remains usable; graph-only scope is never widened and a missing exhaustive Ticket priority filter is not claimed as supported or complete, even after bounded sibling repository evidence

acceptance_scenarios.given: a root goal that bundles several separate questions, whether no capability matched it (jev_none), routing could not choose one capability for it (ambiguous), or routing would accept it as one decision (bundled_accepted)
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: a split is offered for it instead of one decision being formed, recording the goal verbatim with found_at routing, work_item_depth 0 and the routing result

acceptance_scenarios.given: a compound subject
acceptance_scenarios.when: Claude Code proposes the split through host.decompose_goal
acceptance_scenarios.then: 2 to 5 parts are proposed, each quoting verbatim the span of the subject it covers, naming the parts it depends on (no cycles) and the capability that will run it, and the run waits for a human answer with no part run

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you approve it as shown
acceptance_scenarios.then: every part is kept, the answer is recorded with gate_by human:<name> and the time, and the parts are released to run in dependency order; no part runs before a human answer

acceptance_scenarios.given: an approved split whose part p2 depends on part p1
acceptance_scenarios.when: the parts run
acceptance_scenarios.then: they run one at a time as children of the same run, p1 settles before p2 starts, and p1's result is passed to p2 as precedent evidence whose applicability Jev still judges

acceptance_scenarios.given: an approved split whose parts are settling in dependency order
acceptance_scenarios.when: you look at the split's progress, or the run ends
acceptance_scenarios.then: each part shows its outcome (pending, decided, answered or not run) with a link to its child decision record or research result, and the run report's split section has one line per part, starting with the part id and naming its outcome

acceptance_scenarios.given: a single question that routing can give to one capability
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: no split is started and the run goes on as one decision from the precedent step

acceptance_scenarios.given: a single question that no capability can handle
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: no split is started: the run records the capability gap exactly as today and is never sent to the split gate

acceptance_scenarios.given: a caller-supplied decision request (leafcutter.decision_request.v1) that names its own question, options and criteria, even one whose question bundles several questions
acceptance_scenarios.when: routing runs on the run's root
acceptance_scenarios.then: it is never checked for bundling, no split is offered and no Decomposition is written, and the run goes ahead as the one decision the caller named

acceptance_scenarios.given: a work item below the run's root that holds a multi-part decision question or a research request with several needs
acceptance_scenarios.when: the run reaches that work item
acceptance_scenarios.then: a split is started for it with found_at mid_run, its work-item depth (1 or more) and no routing trigger, and it goes to the same split gate

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed part whose quoted span is not in the subject text
acceptance_scenarios.when: the proposal is turned into the split
acceptance_scenarios.then: that part is left out of the parts and shown at the gate read-only with its reason, and it cannot be approved or run

acceptance_scenarios.given: a request offered for a split
acceptance_scenarios.when: the host's proposal holds fewer than 2 parts, counted after any part whose quote is not in the request is set aside
acceptance_scenarios.then: no split gate is shown and no part is created, and the request goes on as a single question according to why the split was offered: with trigger jev_none the run records the capability gap and ends blocked, as today; with trigger ambiguous today's clarification question is asked and the run is waiting_human for the person's answer, with no capability gap recorded unless the request ends unresolved; with trigger bundled_accepted it goes ahead as one decision, and found mid-run the item goes ahead as one

acceptance_scenarios.given: a bundled goal for which the host proposes seven parts, each quoting its words from the goal
acceptance_scenarios.when: the proposal is turned into the split
acceptance_scenarios.then: the split gate offers the first five parts for approval and lists the other two read-only as not covered by this split, each with its text and quote, to be asked again as a request of their own, and they can be neither ticked nor run

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you edit a part's text or untick some parts, then approve
acceptance_scenarios.then: an edited part runs with your text and the record keeps the proposed text beside it, and an unticked part is recorded as left out and never runs

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split of a root goal for which no capability matched (trigger jev_none), shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you reject it
acceptance_scenarios.then: no part runs, the run ends blocked and records the capability gap as it does today, and its report says plainly that the split was rejected and nothing was decided

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split of a root goal for which routing could not choose one capability (trigger ambiguous), shown on the split gate
acceptance_scenarios.when: you reject it
acceptance_scenarios.then: no part runs and the run does not end blocked: today's clarification question is asked ("I am not sure how to handle this request: ... Which of these fits best? You can also say it in your own words."), the run is waiting_human for your answer, no capability gap is recorded unless the request ends unresolved (you cannot be asked, or the follow-up limit is reached), and the report keeps one plain line saying a split was offered and rejected

acceptance_scenarios.given: a proposed split shown on the split gate, offered for a root goal routing would have accepted as one decision (trigger bundled_accepted) or for a work item found mid-run
acceptance_scenarios.when: you reject it
acceptance_scenarios.then: no part runs, the subject or item goes ahead as one decision or research step exactly as without a split, the run is not blocked, and the report keeps one plain line saying a split was offered and rejected

acceptance_scenarios.given: an approved split whose parts p2 and p3 wait for p1 and whose part p4 waits for none
acceptance_scenarios.when: p1 runs but does not settle (it reaches its budget stop, ends blocked, hits a capability gap or is cancelled)
acceptance_scenarios.then: p1 is shown as not settled with its stop reason, p2 and p3 are not run and each names p1 as the part it waited for, p4 still runs, and the run ends partial with the split ended_partial, never completed

Matches leafcutter/decisions v4 state rejected_kept_whole (whole_decision_id), sample dcp-decision-records-bundled. One acceptance scenario; no ACs linked.
